item.content:encoded:
About 12, slipping someone a glass of acid almost surely won't kill them. It would burn like hell instantly and you would spit it out and run to the nearest faucet. Worst case, if you can't get to a sink fast enough your mouth and lips would be disfigured for the rest of your life. But you wouldn't die.

I once picked up a spoon and put it in my mouth assuming it was sugar, but a certain someone I won't name accidentally left a spoon with some granules of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) in the kitchen. A strong base which heats up to near boiling when it dissolves in water, and also dissolves human cells turning the membranes into soap and denaturing the proteins. It hurt like hell and I spit it out and got to the sink in about 4 seconds and rinsed my mouth, and my tongue and the lip where I spit it out was burned and hurt for a few days, but it was nothing horrible and left no lasting damage.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This didn't really do anything for me. It feels a bit too much "fan fiction"…which is the point of Tales, I get, but which in this case felt more like an opportunity for self-reference than an avenue for exploring ideas spun off from the Foundation. It makes it seem more like play pretend than a narrative, is how I suppose I'd phrase that? If the 05s didn't map onto members of the site I think that'd help address that criticism for me, though I appreciate that'd be a bit self-defeating for what you were doing here.

As far as the rest goes, some other comments in the discussion touch on my problems with it. The conceit is very early James Bond, which you even reference in the piece itself, but the actual storytelling is too somber to work as satire, and the self-aware darkness of the humor undercuts it as an honest "bad guys in volcanoes" gothic drama. The absurdity is too gentle; I think you either needed to commit more to the inherent goofiness of it, or go for broke and play it as straight-faced as one can play a supervillain story. Certainly I think the Foundation mythos has some ore to mine there.

Other than my problems with the concept I think the writing itself is pretty good, and the formatting with the O5s (and particularly the way it echoes in the companion piece) works well.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Wow. This is excellent.

It's especially impressive that this story details all the O5s (not just a few), and all the methods of their death, and it manages to make all of them either interesting or outright fascinating.

Also, major bonus points for not making all of them (or even the vast majority) white dudes. I would have forgiven that cliche (and I expected it to go that way, frankly), considering how well executed the story is and how memorable the characters are, but the fact that it doesn't go there makes me like this even more. Awesome all around.

(Yes, there are typos scattered throughout, but it's a testament to the strength of the story that they never seriously bothered me.)
